market_holds: Spot 218.26 (sealed 18:08 UTC 11-23; the stock was 215.17 on the intraday bar, +4.7% on a day SPY rallied about +4.9%). Option-implied event move 11.3% (Dec straddle 19.0% net of ordinary vol, ATM IV 89%); median of the last 7 reactions 9.8%, and they alternate in sign (+15.8, -5.8, -4.6, +9.8, -4.1, +25.8, -11.6). The stock is -59% from its May high of $535 and -31% since the 8-26 close (311): MTZ -35%, GLW -28%, SPY -6% and PWR -1% over the same period. Run-up -4.5% over 20 days, +1.3% over 5. Most of the fall since August came with the AI and data-center tape: 11-05 DY -9.2% with SPY -4.4% (S&P's worst day since April 2025, on midterm data-center moratorium fears), 10-22 DY -5.2% with PWR and GLW -8%, and 11-20 DY -7.1% with SPY -3.6%. Two company-tied legs: 10-21 DY -5.8% while SPY rose, the day AT&T cut its 2027-28 capital investment to $22-23B a year (about $1B below plan, partly the Mexico sale, partly 'fiber build efficiencies'; the 60M fiber target is kept), and 10-30 DY -5.0% while MTZ rose 4.6% on MasTec's call (communications revenue -11.8%, customers deferring wireless and wireline capex amid 4th-carrier speculation and customer reorganizations, 'some vendor slowdown in CapEx in 27'). Consensus Q3 EPS $4.56 on revenue $1.92B (Earnings Whispers 11-16), drifted down from $4.67 and sitting at the guide midpoint ($4.33-4.79, revenue $1.90-1.98B, EBITDA $281-302M); whisper $4.80. FY27 guide revenue $7.48-7.66B (the Q2 raise, net of $150M of wireless moved into FY28) implies Q4 revenue of about $1.53-1.79B, midpoint $1.66B. Q4 EPS consensus is unclear: Benzinga shows $2.68, while Chartmill's FY27 $17.57 (10-18) implies about $3.30. Sell-side FY28 estimates rose about 3% over three months (Chartmill) while the price fell 30%, so the price sits far below a stale consensus. Short interest about 4.8% of float (Aug 19, Equibles); open-interest put/call 0.48. The line it trades on: the next-quarter guide and the Communications margin (13.6% in Q2, -134 bp YoY). In August a 14% EPS beat came with a Q3 guide below consensus and the stock fell 11.6%.
view: Dycom guides conservatively and has beaten the top of its own EPS guide every quarter this year: Q1 FY27 $4.42 against a $2.57-2.90 guide, Q2 $5.29 against $4.40-4.82, Q4 FY26 $2.03 against $1.91 consensus. So a Q3 beat (EPS around $4.9-5.2, revenue near the $1.98B top against $1.92B consensus) is close to the base case, and the $4.80 whisper already leans that way. The beat is not the line. The stock trades on the Q4 guide, the FY27 raise or hold, and what management says about Communications margins and FY28 demand. Since August the counterparty evidence has been mixed. Negative: AT&T, the largest customer, trimmed 2027-28 capital investment by about $1B a year; MasTec called wireline and wireless capex deferrals and a slower 2027 for carriers. Positive: AT&T's 60M fiber target is unchanged and it is on track for 40M+ by year-end; Verizon held 2026 capex at $16-16.5B and expects 32M+ fiber passings; Lumen's PCF deals passed $13.5B and it hit 5M fiber miles early; MasTec booked 2,100 hyperscaler fiber miles and expects meaningful award activity. Both negatives were already priced on their own dates (-5.8% and -5.0% idiosyncratic days). The rest of the fall rides the AI-infrastructure tape, which this release cannot settle. A beat with a full-year raise and a record backlog is the likeliest output and argues mildly for up from a depressed base. The unknown, and the history of alternating reactions, is the Q4 guide: Q4 is the seasonal low, consensus for it is ambiguous ($2.68 vs about $3.30), and this management guided below consensus in August. On a name with beta near 2 to an index that moved 3-5% on several recent days, the tape between 16:00 and 13:00 ET can rival the event. I lean slightly up and do not recommend.
unpriced: Possibly an asymmetry: the price has de-rated about 30% since August on two counterparty read-throughs and the AI tape, while Dycom's own track record (large beats against its own guides, FY raises in Q1 and Q2) and its fiber customers' disclosures (targets unchanged) do not show deterioration in the current quarter. But the Q4 guide, the line the stock trades on, cannot be estimated with any confidence, so this is a lean and not an edge.

recommendation.reason: A Q3 beat is likely given the company's habit of clearing the top of its guide, and the two company-tied negatives since August (AT&T's capex trim, MasTec's communications deferrals) were each priced on their own day. The deciding line, the Q4 guide and the Communications margin trajectory, is not visible, and the Q4 consensus is ambiguous across sources. This management guided below consensus in August. With beta near 2 in a volatile AI tape, the evidence does not reach 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 EPS guide midpoint well below about $2.7-3.3, or a further YoY decline in the Communications margin with cautious FY28 wireline or AT&T commentary, would make this a down print despite a Q3 beat. A FY27 raise with Q4 above $3 and a backlog well above $12.2B would make it a strong up.

self_critique: Against the slight up lean: Dycom guides conservatively, and in this seasonally weak Q4, with AT&T trimming capex and MasTec flagging carrier deferrals, the Q4 guide could again land below a consensus that may be as high as $3.30. That would repeat August's beat-and-fall. The Communications margin may decline YoY again. In a tape where AI-infrastructure names swing 5-10% on macro, any overnight AI wobble swamps the print. Against a down lean: the stock is at about 13-14x forward on stale rising estimates, and a routine beat-and-raise with record backlog and buyback could easily give +10-15%, as in Nov 2025 and May 2026. Neither side clears 65.
